headline: Tech Stocks Poised to Drop as Amazon Adds to AI Spending Fears
author: Emily Forgash

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Tech stocks are set to plunge at the market open on Friday for the second day in a row as fears around AI spending collide with disappointing earnings in big tech's core businesses.
Most Read from Bloomberg

Investors are showing waning tolerance for tech companies that are seeing their legacy businesses falter, especially given their massive capital expenditure plans. Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc.'s results spiked fears that those core segments are being cannibalized by the very technology the firms are betting the house on.
Contracts on the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index fell 2.6% as of 9:06 a.m. in New York, while S&P 500 futures slipped 1.1%.

Amazon shares slumped 7.2% in premarket trading, as the company's AI spending plans and lagging e-commerce business overshadowed solid growth in cloud sales in the eyes of investors after it reported earnings on Thursday. The results dragged all of the Magnificent 7 lower.

The market reacted similarly to Alphabet's results on Wednesday. The Google parent reported search and advertising sales that reinforced investor concerns about AI's threat to its core business, sending its shares down 13% at the close Thursday — the biggest drop ever for the stock — while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4%.

"The weakness in their core businesses is a new wrinkle in the debate about whether the ROI on AI is going to come quickly enough to justify euphoria surrounding this technology," said Matt Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak & Co.

Meanwhile, Intel Corp. is eyeing its worst one-day drop on record after the chipmaker reported a revenue forecast that missed analysts' estimates, hurt by sputtering demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems with its lucrative data center components. Shares fell 26% in premarket trading.

Intel's rivals Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Nvidia Corp. were down 9.3% and 2.4% respectively in premarket trading, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell 6.7%. Dell Technologies Inc., which makes PCs, fell 12% premarket.

Overall, the recent results could be enough to wipe out the Nasdaq 100's gains at the beginning of this week. The market had initially reacted positively to a slew of big tech news, including Anthropic PBC's highly-anticipated initial public offering filing, Meta Platforms Inc.'s more than $95 billion capital raise, and SpaceX's $40 billion equipment-finance lease to pay for AI chip purchases.
All that rosiness has now turned to fear as the market assesses if it can stomach an AI infrastructure buildout that is turning free cash flows negative and that relies on heavy borrowing.

"The bigger question that still remains is will the weakness in tech spillover to the broad market, or can the game of musical chairs continue?" Jonathan Krinsky, chief market technician at BTIG, wrote in a note. "A correlation-one style selloff continues to be elusive, but the set-up for it into November is now more likely, in our view."
For now, investors are looking toward other parts of the market. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index gained 1.2% on Thursday, while around 400 stocks in the benchmark index were positive.
But tech's heavy weighting in both stock indexes could start to erode them, especially in the face of uncertainty surrounding the midterm elections next week.

"If the major averages start to fall, investors will likely start to rotate towards cash instead of other sectors, especially with all of the 'bubble' talk they've heard over the past year," Maley said.

Other areas of tech are being punished, too. Roblox Corp. shares fell 14% in premarket trading after reporting daily active users that came in below estimates, and Reddit Inc. shares slumped 23% after announcing plans to limit access to its online user forums to users with accounts.

Outside of tech, ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. reported earnings before the bell on Friday that surpassed expectations on the strength of surging gasoline and diesel prices that pushed refining results to an all-time high. The shares gained 1.7% in premarket trading. Chevron Corp. also beat expectations, sending shares up 1.4%.
Sectors in Focus

• Cryptocurrency-linked stocks fell in premarket trading after Binance suffered the industry's biggest-ever hack amid growing worries about risks posed by hackers in the age of AI. Bitcoin slumped 2.0%.
